reasons: The excerpt expressly conditions the provider's full comprehensive audit on working with them “on the higher side” and being over 300,000 sessions.
It also supports the stated audit duration and approximate 100-page findings document.
The excerpt directly states that test duration should typically last two to four weeks.
The candidate retains the source's qualifier that this is typical rather than absolute.
The source says it likes to run the comprehensive, over-300,000-session test for at least two weeks to reduce the effect of external factors.
The weekday coverage is presented as an example in both the source and candidate, rather than as a mandatory completion criterion.
The source explicitly says statistical significance is important but that power is more important.
It describes power as requiring a sufficiently large data set to show that the test is proven to make more money; the candidate does not introduce an unsupported numeric threshold.
The excerpt says that after conducting the research, the speaker's team creates a framework and uses the PXL framework.
It explicitly states that the framework is not theirs and that they do not claim to have invented it.
For high-volume stores conducting small tests at velocity, the source permits concurrent homepage and cart tests because they are far apart, and permits above-fold with below-fold testing.
The candidate accurately marks the 80% above-fold focus as the speaker's reported internal practice rather than an established universal allocation.
The source recounts that winning tests were overwritten after new leadership became involved and that the team is restoring them.
It also says that a win usually persists “into perpetuity”; the candidate keeps this as part of the specific anecdote rather than claiming a defined preservation process.
The source says comprehensive-audit findings can be used not only on site, but also in ads and retention.
Its dependency on the comprehensive-audit unit is consistent with the surrounding source context.
The source directly states that a good CRO testing tool will tell users statistical significance.
The candidate does not add tool names, calculation methods, or a claim that significance alone establishes a winning test.
The surrounding excerpt says that bugs can occur despite an in-house development and QA function and despite AI assistance.
It advises QA before launch, including repeating QA two or three times; the candidate accurately preserves this as a warning rather than inventing QA procedures.

source_limitations: The excerpt begins mid-sentence and refers to “these two things” and to “bolded” non-negotiables that are not present in the supplied text.
The excerpt ends mid-sentence at “Generates over eight,” so the associated revenue figure and its unit cannot be determined from this source.

This is a spoken presentation transcript with apparent transcription errors and ambiguous phrasing; several operational claims are presented as the speaker's or firm's practices rather than independently established requirements.
